coverageNote: Five audit units covered all 33 current Markdown sources: 02.01 (8), 02.02 (6), 02.03 (5), 02.04 (6), and domain-level credit feature and cross-cut surfaces (8). Each source received 3a implementer simulation, 3b rubric scoring, and 3c devil's-advocate probing across all eight rubric dimensions.

findings.claim: The mandatory contested embargo-lift SLA has no numeric target or capacity measure, so the status quo can persist without a measurable resolution point.

evidence.excerpt: D-21 makes an SLA mandatory ... The requirement is specified; the number is not, and neither dependency budgets for this load.

findings.forcedInvention: A contested-lift resolution deadline and the capacity behavior when the dispute queue cannot meet it.
findings.failureScenario: A Producer can keep a work embargoed by challenging each lift while no service target requires the platform to resolve the challenge.

findings.claim: The leak-or-bootleg exception has a User owner and deferred stage but no deadline; it blocks the authorised-release predicate needed to decide an evidence-based embargo lift.

evidence.excerpt: The open-question table contains Question, Owner, and Deferred To columns, with no deadline column.
No source defines an authorised-vs-unauthorised predicate; the human route has no defined test to apply.

findings.forcedInvention: Whether public reachability from a leak or bootleg is sufficient to lift embargo, and the authority and test for that decision.
findings.failureScenario: A reviewer either exposes an unauthorised recording or leaves a legitimately released credit embargoed by applying an invented rule.

findings.claim: Shell consent has a User owner and deferred security stage but no deadline; it blocks pre-claim visibility, objection, and refusal behavior for people who never signed up.

evidence.excerpt: The open-question table contains Question, Owner, and Deferred To columns, with no deadline column.
Adding a non-user by name creates a record about a person who never agreed to be on the platform; visibility and objection path are open.
What is publicly visible on an unclaimed shell before anyone claims it?

findings.forcedInvention: The consent basis, default visibility, objection route, and outcome when a non-user refuses a shell containing other parties' assertions.
findings.failureScenario: A roll call publishes a professional profile about an uninvolved person with no lawful or product-defined way to contest or suppress it.

findings.claim: Import-source licensing is an owner-held legal gate with no deadline; it blocks the decision of which catalogues may be ingested and redistributed.

evidence.excerpt: Source licence forbids ingestion/redistribution: Hard stop ... legal gate.
The open-question table contains Question, Owner, and Deferred To columns, with no deadline column.
MusicBrainz, Discogs, DDEX and PRO data have materially different terms; some may prohibit the proposed import.

findings.forcedInvention: A legally permitted source list, permitted uses, and required attribution or redistribution restrictions.
findings.failureScenario: The importer ships against an unlicensed catalogue or silently omits sources based on an implementer's unsupported legal judgment.

findings.claim: Import review defines only directional ranking; the exact ranking signals and the surfaced-versus-held cut remain pending, so queue behavior is not implementable without inventing product logic.

evidence.excerpt: Exact ranking signals and the surfaced-vs-held cut are pending while low-confidence rows are held.

findings.forcedInvention: The ranking feature set, threshold or quota, and release conditions for held imported credits.
findings.failureScenario: An importer either floods reviewers with low-confidence credits or indefinitely hides valid credits using an arbitrary cutoff.

findings.claim: Claim contests have no corroboration SLA or alternate true-owner control, leaving both pendency and control of the contested credit unbounded.

evidence.excerpt: Pendency is unbounded in the worst case ... nothing states how long the Unresolvable path takes to establish.
No corroboration SLA exists and the true owner cannot set the line Unlisted; a bound or control is needed before implementation.

findings.forcedInvention: A corroboration deadline, terminal transition, and temporary visibility or control for the credible claimant during pendency.
findings.failureScenario: A first claimant holds a disputed public credit indefinitely while the person who can substantiate ownership cannot hide or correct it.

findings.claim: Ring-detection calibration has a User owner and deferred security stage but no deadline; it blocks activation of score-side demotion without inventing the model's safety-critical values.

evidence.excerpt: The open-question table contains Question, Owner, and Deferred To columns, with no deadline column.
Thresholds, weights, demotion cut, and density floor need real graph-timing data and are deferred as one unit.

findings.forcedInvention: Signal thresholds, composite weights, demotion cut, density floor, and the validation evidence required before enabling the detector.
findings.failureScenario: An implementer enables silent ranking penalties with arbitrary values that either punish real scenes or fail to demote fabricated-credit rings.

findings.unit: Domain-level credit feature and cross-cut surfaces
findings.claim: Imported-credit adjudication has a User owner and deferred stage but no deadline; it blocks whether the adjudicated rung exists for credits with no capture evidence or witnesses.

evidence.excerpt: The ladder has no import carve-out, and the owner-held scope ruling must decide whether adjudication is offered at all.

findings.forcedInvention: Whether imported credits may enter adjudication, and if so the admissibility, evidence, and terminal-outcome rules for that path.
findings.failureScenario: Two implementations diverge: one offers costly quasi-adjudication for imported credits while another rejects the same cases at filing.

findings.unit: Domain-level credit feature and cross-cut surfaces
findings.claim: The canonical taxonomy seed source and licence have a User owner and deferred stage but no deadline; this blocks lawful construction of the Must-have role picker.

evidence.excerpt: DDEX AVS, MusicBrainz, Discogs and PRO role lists have different terms, and some may prohibit picker redistribution.

findings.forcedInvention: The licensed canonical seed, redistribution rights, attribution requirements, and fallback if no candidate source is permitted.
findings.failureScenario: The core taxonomy is seeded from a list the platform cannot legally publish or export, making the role picker and RIN mapping non-compliant.

findings.unit: Domain-level credit feature and cross-cut surfaces
findings.claim: The downstream supersession contract for a stale export has a User owner and deferred stage but no deadline; it blocks the external behavior after an amendment or retraction.

evidence.excerpt: Whether the external consumer is told its prior copy is superseded and accepts a re-send remains open.
After export or royalty registration, downstream consumers hold a stale fact; royalty correction-filing deadline is pending.

findings.forcedInvention: The recipient notification or supersession contract, retry and acknowledgement behavior, and deadline for downstream royalty correction filings.
findings.failureScenario: The exporter re-sends an amended RIN but a label or royalty recipient continues to rely on the prior version with no defined supersession or correction deadline.

findings.unit: Domain-level credit feature and cross-cut surfaces
findings.claim: Gear resale disclosure and consent have a User owner and deferred security stage but no deadline; they block the visibility rule for a prior owner's session history on a marketplace listing.

evidence.excerpt: The open-question table contains Question, Owner, and Deferred To columns, with no deadline column.
The previous owner's session history travels sideways into a marketplace listing and needs a disclosure or consent rule.

findings.forcedInvention: The default exposure, consent model, redaction behavior, and sale-time transfer rule for pre-sale gear-discography history.
findings.failureScenario: Selling a registered item exposes a musician's previously unpublished sessions to prospective buyers without a defined opt-out or disclosure rule.

findings.unit: Domain-level credit feature and cross-cut surfaces
findings.claim: AI disclosure enforcement has a User owner and deferred security stage but no deadline; it blocks whether missing disclosure can prevent export or release.

evidence.excerpt: The open-question table contains Question, Owner, and Deferred To columns, with no deadline column.
The platform must decide whether disclosure blocks export or release or remains voluntary.

findings.forcedInvention: The enforcement policy, affected export and release surfaces, exemptions, and response when an external recipient mandates disclosure.
findings.failureScenario: One implementation permits an undisclosed AI-assisted release that a DSP rejects, while another blocks a release without product authorization.
